open_issues.impact: P5.12/ADR-0031 and the reviewer should know these behaviours
open_issues.text: Detail choices (D44, implementation level): (1) the hub's local expiry stays strict at exp by its own clock (no hub.clock_skew added), so a revoked writer whose control message is lost stops within token_ttl of the last token the backend issued (<= token_ttl + clock_skew as documented); (2) recheck none closes with a code by reason: generation 4409, gone 4404, token 4001, revoked/unavailable/other 4403; an unknown access value makes the connection read-only; (3) a renewal never upgrades read to write within a session (it would need a reconnect); (4) registration happens in `connected` because Hocuspocus 4.3 onAuthenticate has no live connection; onAuthenticate takes a registry control mark before the backend call, and a connection that authenticated while a control message for its drive (or a global one) went by is rechecked once it registers; (5) every control message triggers a recheck (no skipping by permissions_version: token mint reads rights and versions non-atomically); (6) POST /control answers 202 before the recheck finishes, 409 for a replayed signature (kept for 2x tolerance), 422 for a signed unreadable message, 401 for missing/stale/wrong signatures and when the hub has no webhook secret.

open_issues.next: P5.12: handle forbidden nacks and the close codes above; optionally a per-connection status reason later
open_issues.text: For P5.12 (vue-collaboration): a writer made read-only gets no new status message. It learns from `nack {code: forbidden, retry: false}` on its envelopes, and Hocuspocus answers its sync writes with SyncStatus(false). Close codes the client must handle: 4403 forbidden (revoked, or renewal refused), 4409 epoch_changed, 4404 document_gone, 4001 token expired (ask for a new session). The hub renews the token in its own connection context only; the browser provider keeps its original token, so a reconnect after exp gets 4001 and must fetch a new session.
